title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: whole saving will includes vocation according to purpose — true praedestinans will
pass_a_gloss: For the whole will of God concerning the salvation of men is not contained in such a decree, Whoever will have believed will have eternal life. For in the sacred Scriptures God has moreover opened that he wills to gift to certain ones, of whom from mere good pleasure he wills to have mercy before others, a vocation according to purpose; from such vocation repentance, faith, sanctification, and finally glorification, and all these things infallibly. This will of God is the true and properly predestinating will, and is opened in the Gospel as to the thing, although the individuals as to name are not there expressed. These things concerning the Major.
pass_b_english: For God's whole will about men's salvation is not contained in Whoever believes will have eternal life. Scripture further opens that to certain ones — of whom from mere good pleasure he wills to have mercy before others — he wills to gift vocation according to purpose; from that vocation repentance, faith, sanctification, and finally glorification, all infallibly. That is the true, properly predestinating will, opened in the Gospel as to the thing, though individuals are not there named. So much for the Major.
source_text: Tota siquidem Dei voluntas de salute hominum non continetur tali decreto, Qui crediderit habebit vitam aeternam. Nam in sacris Scripturis Deus insuper patefecit, se quibusdam, quorum ex mero beneplacito vult prae aliis misereri, velle donare vocationem secundum propositum; ex tali vocatione poenitentiam, fidem, sanctificationem, et demum glorificationem, atque haec omnia infallibiliter. Haec voluntas Dei est vera et proprie voluntas praedestinans, estque in Evangelio patefacta quoad rem, quamvis individua quoad nomen non inibi exprimantur. Haec de Majore.
